imageBase: A full-bleed portrait 9:16 frame from an exquisitely illustrated South Indian wedding invitation film. Premium dimensional storybook illustration: lifelike richly carved architecture, soft cinematic atmospheric perspective, and elegant subtly cartoon-stylized people; not a flat poster or photograph. A single warm sandstone Dravidian temple complex at golden sunrise. Sandstone is aged honey-beige with dark brown carved recesses, not metallic gold. Tall pyramidal nine-tier gopuram with seven small finials; the SAME shape vocabulary throughout. Brass lamps, small ritual fires, incense wisps, orange marigolds, white jasmine and green mango leaves; cream, warm ochre, deep red and antique gold palette. Sunlight from camera-left makes long diagonal shadows and moving-camera specular potential on polished stone and brass. Rich depth with close carved foreground columns, midground subject, distant receding architecture. Delicate warm bloom, cinematic contrast, restrained highlights, realistic tiny bevel reflections. The small central Ganesha mantap is a freestanding square open pavilion, four thick carved square pillars, flat stone roof with a small stepped pyramidal cap, a lotus carving centered on the front lintel, three shallow front steps, orange-and-white garland scallops, and a dark doorway already containing a small seated orange-gold Ganesha idol. This low mantap is distinct from the giant gopuram behind it. No extra temple tower, giant doorway floating in the sky, frames, watermark or interface. Use only the wording explicitly requested for this shot. Create solely from this written description.

scenes.name: Aerial aimed at the existing small mantap

The tall main gopuram rises in the upper center at the far end. The SMALL four-pillared Ganesha mantap described above is clearly visible in the CENTER-LOWER part, directly between the camera and the tower. Its entire low roof, three front steps and OPEN DARK FRONT ENTRANCE are unobstructed; its roof spans about 23 percent of frame width, and its front doorway sits near x=50%, y=66%. A tiny seated Ganesha and lamp glow are ALREADY visible inside that dark front entrance. This is the exact physical destination of an upcoming forward diving camera flight: give the camera an unobstructed straight route across the foreground and through that doorway. A small rectangular water tank is near the lower edge, NOT hiding the pavilion. Long side colonnades, palms beyond the compound, sparse incense plumes. Sunrise at upper left, hazy distant horizon. Monumental tower behind the smaller mantap, not two giant towers. No legible text. Few distant devotees at the far sides only. Clear architectural proportions, intimate little mandap inside a vast courtyard.

scenes.name: Inside that mantap, live blessing arrival
scenes.prompt: Camera is NOW INSIDE the small square Ganesha mantap, a few meters past its front steps, at standing eye level. Symmetrical frontal composition with two close square carved pillars at the extreme edges and the flat carved lotus lintel across the top. This is a modest open-sided pavilion with roughly six-meter-high columns, not another towering temple facade. A beautiful seated Ganesha idol is centered in the lower middle on a flower-covered waist-high pedestal. The SAME nine-tier gopuram remains outside behind the idol, visible THROUGH THE REAR OPENING, softly hazed by sunrise. The left side passage opens onto an adjoining courtyard bay, allowing a leftward orbit out of the pavilion. On the upper carved lintel, exact gold devotional text in two lines: 'Om Shree' / 'Ganeshaya Namah'. Text occupies no more than the upper 18% of the image. Sunbeam enters from left, lights incense smoke, glints on brass lamps, reflects on the brown polished stone floor. Capture a celebration at the camera's slowdown: many airborne white jasmine petals and orange marigold petals at near, middle and far depths; several large out-of-focus petals very close to the lens at the top corners, sharp midground petals spiraling beside the idol, tiny distant gold sparks. Keep the face and lettering clear. The composition has enough surrounding floor and columns for a gentle ongoing push toward the idol.

scenes.name: Invitation in west-side courtyard bay
scenes.prompt: Eye-level camera in the open courtyard bay immediately to the LEFT of the Ganesha mantap, facing diagonally back toward the same distant nine-tier gopuram. A massive garlanded square column occupies the extreme right foreground, its side face visible to establish an arrival from a LEFTWARD camera orbit. Two rows of carved columns and elephant-shaped stone balustrades recede behind. Center a slightly aged ivory invitation board on a square antique-gold plinth; marigolds and white jasmine form a delicate frame. The board and pedestal together occupy the central lower 52% of the picture, not the entire image. Render exact highly legible ornate gold lettering: 'Bodha’s' / 'Wedding' / 'Invitation', each on its own line. Tiny gold emblem above, restrained flourish below. Brass standing lamps at several depths, small diyas along the floor, realistic warm reflections. Camera left sunlight catches the board edge and foreground pillar. Many white and orange petals flutter in the air at staggered depths, near-lens petal bokeh at the upper edge and tiny golden specks near the floor. An open aisle stretches backward toward the camera and connects to the groom's long pillared hall on camera-right. No people in the foreground. The small Ganesha mantap is offscreen to camera-right and must NOT be drawn in the background. This is a distinct side bay: center the invitation board on its decorated plinth, with only the distant tall tower behind and the side colonnades leading toward it. No small structure between board and tower. Preserve all three exact text lines and the rich airborne petals.

scenes.name: Groom with dimensional luminous name

An appealing adult Indian groom rendered as polished storybook animation: slightly enlarged expressive almond eyes, smooth sculpted cheeks, clean simplified facial planes, stylized swept black hair, no pores, no photographic face or stubble. This must unmistakably look like a dimensional animated wedding illustration, with a believable adult body. He wears a traditional IVORY SILK DHOTI and a gold-bordered ANGAVASTRAM draped diagonally across a BARE CHEST and one shoulder. No shirt, no kurta, no jacket. A few fine gold necklaces. He stands relaxed full-length on the LEFT, his figure about 62 percent of frame height. The rest is an intricate illustrated sandstone temple corridor: close square carved pillars, long receding rows, golden sunrise shafts, hanging orange-white garlands and brass lamps. On the RIGHT at chest height, suspended in air, gorgeous flowing beveled GOLD CALLIGRAPHY reads exactly Chi. above Ashok above Kumar. Elegant thin expressive strokes, not a thick block font. Letters have a slightly turned 3D angle, intensely luminous fine edges, metal reflections, subtle bloom and a sparkling finishing light trail under Kumar. Tiny golden sparks shed from the flourish and warm light reflects onto the stone below. An abundant shower of rotating white jasmine petals, orange marigold petals and delicate gold flakes, at near-lens defocused foreground, sharp midground and tiny distant depths. Enough empty space around the figure and title to read both clearly. Warm illustrated cinematic materials throughout. COMPOSITION REQUIREMENT: a roofed corridor entirely fills the background, its ceiling and rows of columns converge deep into the hall. There is NO outside tower or shrine behind him. The groom is head-to-toe within the left third with generous 10 percent margins above and below, about 65 percent of frame height, not a cropped or huge closeup. Maintain natural adult proportions and age, lightly stylized confident warm face, not childlike. Keep all name lettering inside the right two thirds with a clear margin from the right edge.

videoBase: A single continuous physically motivated cinematic FPV camera move in the same illustrated South Indian temple. The supplied first and last images are precise anchors; preserve the recognizable architecture and spatial relationships between them. The shot must have a clear speed ramp: calm anticipation, a SHORT explosive travel burst with directional edge motion blur and fast close-foreground parallax, then strong smooth deceleration into living slow motion. Never spread the travel evenly across the whole shot. During slow motion the camera still drifts subtly, smoke curls, brass highlights slide with viewing angle, floor reflections shift, and layered petals tumble. Around the arrival, a fresh gust releases MANY white jasmine and orange marigold petals: small softly defocused individual petals pass near the lens, crisp midground petals rotate independently, tiny distant petals and gold sparks drift more slowly. These are SMALL SINGLE loose curled petals, never whole flowers, daisies, flower heads or discs. Each petal is at most 2-4 percent of frame width, and no motif obscures faces or letters. The world stays solid and grounded: camera travels through existing open routes; do not create a new facade, shrink the whole temple, dissolve rooms, or morph subjects into signs. Strong depth and changing perspective, stable horizon except for the small motivated bank described below. Preserve the exact readable final lettering. Ambient motion continues through the final frame. No cut, crossfade, static slideshow, uniform-speed sideways slide, or full orbit.

clips.prompt: FORWARD DIVE THROUGH THE EXISTING SMALL MANTAP. Keep the same tall gopuram BEHIND the small center-lower mantap throughout the approach. 0.0-0.8s: a gentle forward aerial drift establishes the courtyard; identify the tiny glowing Ganesha already inside the small pavilion's dark open entrance. 0.8-1.9s: accelerate sharply FORWARD AND DOWN directly at THAT small pavilion. Its roof, columns and entrance grow rapidly toward the lens; the water tank passes BELOW the camera and the tall rear gopuram moves UPWARD toward the top edge. The camera moves closer, never backward. 1.9-2.4s: skim above the three steps and fly THROUGH THE EXISTING DARK DOORWAY UNDER its lotus lintel. Near pillars whip past left and right with directional blur; the roof passes overhead. Do not introduce a second pavilion or replace the main tower. 2.4-3.0s: level at seated-idol height and brake very smoothly into the supplied interior Ganesha composition, keeping the original tower outside behind the idol. 3.0-6.0s: a very slow elegant forward creep, gentle smoke, shimmering brass, and a celebratory shower of white/orange petals growing richer after deceleration. Devotional text 'Om Shree Ganeshaya Namah' is already carved above the idol and is revealed by entering the pavilion. Ganesha remains the same stationary idol seen through the entrance, not a newly appearing foreground object. Critical corrections: the entire accelerated approach is a short dynamic burst; by 2.5 seconds the camera has passed the doorway and has begun braking. Never pause on the approach keyframe. After arrival, keep airborne pieces tiny and naturally petal-shaped; no large floating five-petaled flowers. The physical mantap gets larger continuously until its columns pass outside the frame. The idol has always stood at the back of this same small open pavilion. Do not make an extra doorway appear inside it.

LEFTWARD CURVING WHIP REVEAL, DIFFERENT FROM THE OPENING DIVE. 0.0-0.3s: complete a tiny slow forward creep toward the Ganesha pedestal. 0.3-1.25s: accelerate into a decisive LEFTWARD camera arc through the open left side of the mantap, banking only about 4 degrees. Ganesha and his pedestal sweep toward SCREEN RIGHT and leave view. Pivot left around the very close square column; that foreground column whips across the lens with natural directional blur. The camera physically translates and turns, not a flat rightward slide. 1.25-1.9s: the ivory invitation board enters from SCREEN LEFT at an oblique angle; counter-steer gently and level the horizon, easing strongly into its centered frontal composition. 1.9-5.0s: continue a tiny slow push, with a sun glint traveling over the gilded frame and brass lamps. An abundant fresh petal shower blooms into the view on arrival and floats down in several depth layers, white petals and orange marigolds against the architecture. The board is already physically present in its courtyard bay. Its text is exactly 'Bodha’s Wedding Invitation', held stable and readable as the camera settles.

BACKWARD RELEASE, RIGHT TURN, AND GOLD-LIGHT NAME REVEAL. 0.0-0.65s: accelerate BACKWARD away from the invitation board down the stone aisle; the board recedes in perspective and more ceiling and floor enter the picture. 0.65-1.45s: bank slightly and whip-turn RIGHT about 65 degrees into the pillared groom corridor while still moving backward. Nearby pillars cross fast, the invitation courtyard exits screen left, strong parallax and brief directional blur. 1.45-2.4s: brake into the groom composition. During this turning arrival, a brilliant THIN EDGE-ON VERTICAL GOLD STREAK ignites in the empty air on the right of the corridor; it broadens and unfurls into the exact ornate calligraphy 'Chi. Ashok Kumar'. The reveal is luminous flowing calligraphic strokes and changing three-dimensional viewing angle, not a flat fade or a name board. Gold bloom peaks briefly as the strokes trace on, then relaxes to glossy beveled gold so the complete name is readable by 2.4s. Small gold sparks shed from the finishing flourish and illuminate the nearby floor. The groom is already standing to the left and is uncovered by the moving column, never materializes or walks in. 2.4-5.0s: a gentle sideways arc of just a few degrees plus tiny backward drift gives changing reflections across the completed 3D letters. He gives a restrained natural blink and small smile. A rich shower of white jasmine, orange petals and delicate gold flakes tumbles in layered slow motion as the camera decelerates; smoke and lamp flames remain alive. End with his full body on the left and the complete luminous gold name on the right.
